flags.detail: Keyed option A describes the mitigation as 'letting one request rebuild the entry under a lock while the others serve the stale value'. In the scenario as stated the key has expired, so in a plain TTL cache there is no stale value left to serve; serving stale during rebuild requires an additional design (soft TTL / stale-while-revalidate / probabilistic early expiration) the stem does not posit. The key is still the only correct option — cache stampede is unambiguously right and B, C, D are clearly wrong — but a strong candidate can be snagged by the half-sentence. The explanation itself is accurate (lock plus TTL jitter), so option and explanation are out of step.
flags.suggested_fix: Reword option A to '...letting one request rebuild the entry under a lock while the others wait or serve a retained stale copy, and by jittering expiry times' — or drop the stale-serving clause, matching the explanation.

flags.detail: Option B, 'Register /reports/:id as a server-side route that renders the report itself', would in fact stop the 404 on reload — it is server-side rendering, a real and widely used answer to the deep-link problem, not a false statement. The stem asks 'What is required?', which overstates the uniqueness of C. C is the intended and minimal SPA answer, and the explanation only rebuts option D (redirect to root), never B.
flags.suggested_fix: Tighten the stem to pin the intent, e.g. '...what is the minimal change to the web server configuration that fixes this while keeping the app a pure client-rendered SPA?', and note in the explanation that server-rendering the route also works but abandons the SPA model.
